world.title: ZAMBIA: Franciscan Family in Zambia Commemorates 800 Years of St. Francis’ Death
world.description:
Ndola Archdiocese Media
The Archdiocese of Ndola in Zambia joined the Franciscan family in commemorating 800 years since the death of St. Francis of Assisi, with a solemn and colorful Eucharistic celebration held at St. John’s Convent School Grounds in Kitwe.
The celebration brought together members of different Franciscan orders and congregations, clergy, religious, and lay faithful, united in honoring the life and spiritual legacy of St. Francis of Assisi, whose example of humility, simplicity, love, and service continues to inspire the Church.
The Holy Mass was presided over by the Archbishop of Ndola, Most Rev. Benjamin Phiri, and concelebrated by the Provincial Minister of the Franciscan Friars for Zambia and Malawi, Rev. Fr. Matthews Kasongo, OFM Conv.
In his homily, Archbishop Phiri spoke about the life of St. Francis, highlighting his total surrender to God and his commitment to living the Gospel wholeheartedly. He reflected on the saint’s defining charisms, particularly humility, love for the poor, fraternity, and a life detached from worldly possessions in favor of serving God and others.
The Archbishop challenged the faithful, especially members of the Franciscan family, to go beyond celebrating the name of St. Francis and genuinely embrace the charisms and values he left behind. He cautioned against honoring the saint through ceremonies alone while failing to put his teachings into practice.
He called on Christians to be authentic witnesses of the Gospel by living lives characterized by fraternity, fidelity, love, and humility.
Archbishop Phiri emphasized that the true way to honor St. Francis is to imitate his example and allow the spirit of the saint to be reflected in everyday relationships, service, and commitment to God.
Meanwhile, during the commemoration, the Conventual Franciscan Friars appealed for financial support toward the construction of a house for their priests.
END

science.title: Integrating hippopotamus optimization algorithm into machine learning frameworks for predicting suspended sediment concentrations
science.description: The vertical distribution of sediment concentration is a fundamental component of sediment transport hydraulics, directly impacting the estimation of sediment loads in riverine and channel systems. Therefore, accurate characterization of this distribution remains a critical challenge in hydraulic engineering. To address this, advanced intelligent modeling techniques offer a robust pathway for reliable prediction. This study evaluates the performance of six distinct modeling approaches—ORELM, ORELM-HOA, GPR, GPR-HOA, GMDH-ANFIS, and GMDH-ANFIS-HOA—to predict the relative sediment concentration distribution (C/Ca​). Results indicated that the integration of meta-heuristic optimization significantly enhances the predictive precision of the GMDH-ANFIS, ORELM, and GPR frameworks. Comparative analysis reveals that the GMDH-ANFIS-HOA model achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding an RMSE of 0.0434 and R2 of 0.9747 during the training phase, and an RMSE of 0.0424 and R2 of 0.9727 during the testing phase. The GPR-HOA model followed as the second-best performer. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis identified the relative depth (y/D) as the most dominant factor influencing model accuracy. These findings demonstrate that the optimized GMDH-ANFIS-HOA model provides a reliable and efficient computational tool for engineers and hydrologists, facilitating improved design and management of irrigation canals, river engineering projects, and sediment-related environmental assessments.
